blocks.text: Why projects fail: the cost of ignored risks

Project management failure examples are rarely the result of a single event. They usually result from small, ignored risks that grow over time. When you ignore a risk, you pay in budget, time, and team morale.
Common causes of risk mitigation failure

items: Invisibility: Risk registers are often static spreadsheets that nobody updates.
Siloed communication: Information stays trapped in email instead of reaching the team.
Lack of ownership: When everyone owns the risk, nobody takes action.
Reactive culture: Teams address problems only after they become full crises.

blocks.text: How to fix risk management on your Mac

You do not need expensive enterprise software to manage risk. Start by making your risk register a living document. Put it in a place where your team actually works, like a shared folder or a project management app.
Assign a specific person to every risk. If a risk has no owner, it is just a complaint. Use a clear due date for the next review of that specific risk.

faq.question: What is the biggest mistake in project risk management?
faq.answer: The biggest mistake is treating the risk register as a one-time task during planning. It must be updated regularly as the project changes.

faq.question: How do I know if my project is failing?
faq.answer: Look for signs like constant scope creep, missed milestones, and team members who cannot explain the current project status.
